newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel group to buy more of United Mizrahi Bank.
newsitem.headline: Israel group to buy more of United Mizrahi Bank.

text.p: Israel's Ofer Wertheim group told the Israeli government it would exercise an option to take 25 percent more shares in United Mizrahi Bank, MI Holdings said on Tuesday.

"The controlling shareholders in Bank Mizrahi announced to the Treasury and MI Holdings their intention to implement the option given them to acquire another 25 percent," a spokeswoman for MI Holdings, the group charged with privatising Israel's banks, told Reuters.
"The formal announcement will be given in the coming days. The expected value is more than 440 million shekels ($129 million)."
The Ofer Wertheim group has a 26 percent controlling stake in the bank, acquired in 1995.
Bank Mizrahi is the only one of Israel's top five banks that is not publicly traded.
The government hopes to float at least 20 percent of the bank on the bourse in the second or third quarter of 1997.
The announcement marks the latest step forward in the government's bank privatisation programme.
A $150 million public offering for Bank Leumi is taking place on Tuesday after a successful institutional pre-sale last week.

In April, Israel's offering of Israel Discount Bank shares and warrants was three times oversubscribed. In addition, the government is undertaking holding a tender now to sell the controlling stake in Bank Hapoalim.
The government hopes to raise three billion shekels from bank privatisation this year.
